answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x during a confirmed daily settlement peak with heavy writes, so the only intervention should absorb load without shedding customer writes. memory_b3 is the closest prior: headroom kept queues flat through a surge. That is a better fit than b1 (rollback of an error spike, not latency), b5 (report/dashboard offload, not evidenced here), b2 (no regional signal), or b4 (fail-fast would drop writes and fights the objective). Release timing is suggestive but incomplete (symptoms started ~30 min later; no error spike). Residual uncertainty: b3 describes pre-peak provisioning, not a mid-peak add, and a bad release could still be causal—hence verify b3 before committing.
